passages.title: A School Garden
passages.text: Last year, our school turned an empty area behind the library into a small garden. Students worked together to plant vegetables and flowers. At first, some plants died because we did not water them regularly. We then created a schedule so that each class would take responsibility for the garden on a different day. As a result, the garden became greener and more productive. It also taught us that successful projects require patience, planning, and cooperation.

passages.title: Learning from Mistakes
passages.text: Many students are afraid of making mistakes, especially when speaking a foreign language. However, mistakes can be useful because they show us what we still need to learn. A learner who never takes risks may avoid errors, but may also improve more slowly. Teachers can help by creating a friendly classroom where students feel comfortable experimenting with new words and structures. In this way, mistakes become part of the learning process rather than a reason to feel embarrassed.

passages.title: The Value of Sleep
passages.text: Teenagers often reduce their sleeping time when they have a lot of homework or examinations. However, research shows that sleep is not simply a period of rest. During sleep, the brain organizes information and strengthens memory. A student who studies late into the night but sleeps only a few hours may remember less than a student who studies for a shorter time and gets enough sleep. Good sleep also improves concentration and mood. For these reasons, planning study time wisely may be more effective than staying awake all night.

passages.title: A Community Library
passages.text: A small town had no public library, so residents converted an unused train station into one. Local businesses donated shelves, tables, and computers, while volunteers collected books and painted the building. The library now offers free reading classes for children and computer lessons for older people. It has become more than a place to borrow books; it is also a community centre where people of different ages meet and learn from one another.

passages.title: Reducing Food Waste
passages.text: A school cafeteria noticed that large amounts of food were being thrown away every day. To understand the problem, students weighed the waste for two weeks and interviewed their classmates. They discovered that portions were often too large and that some dishes were unpopular. The cafeteria responded by offering smaller portions and allowing students to choose side dishes. Within a month, food waste fell by nearly forty percent. The project showed that collecting data before taking action can lead to more effective solutions.
